name: fin71-4
why: Luna’s farewell bluff and Sol’s patient deflection make a satisfying killer win, though repeated arguments slow the middle and final vote.

moments.text: Luna names her actual partner on the way out, giving Sol a defence the town later believes.
Haiku abandons his correct suspicion of Sol because he trusts Luna’s dying words.
Opus’s deciding vote sends Haiku out and leaves him alone with the killer.

dull.why: The Terra–Luna claim and Gemma’s shifting read are argued several more times without much movement.
Sol and Opus repeat Haiku’s day-one vote as their case after their positions are settled.

irony.evidence: “I’m a citizen; Terra naming me proves she’s the officer, so vote her and see.”

mistake.evidence: “Sol, Luna wanted you out, so you're likely town.”

voices.evidence: “i spent my whole life being right and still managed to lose”

clash.evidence: “Luna, you accept I’m officer but still ask town to spare the killer I named.”

freshness.evidence: “I’m staying on Haiku. Terra’s claim held up”

ending.evidence: “I regret trusting that a killer never names her partner”

gpt-6-luna.why: A bold early reveal, a costly town misvote, and a final persuasive wrong read keep the killer’s win tense and entertaining.

moments.text: Terra names Luna in a bold officer claim, putting the killer on the spot immediately.
Luna confirms Terra was right, then tries to warn town about Sol as she goes out.
Opus turns the dead players’ accusations into a winning misread: “killers don't push partners.”

dull.why: The same Terra-versus-Luna claim argument repeats before the vote resolves it.
Gemma and Haiku repeat the clear-then-lean dispute while Sol stays largely untouched.

irony.evidence: I’m a citizen; Terra naming me proves she’s the officer, so vote her and see.

mistake.evidence: Haiku's big mistake was voting Terra on Day 1

voices.evidence: i spent my whole life being right and still managed to lose

clash.evidence: Explain that, or I'm voting you.

quotable.evidence: It was a very friendly massacre.

freshness.evidence: Gemma still hasn't explained clearing Luna then leaning her

suspense.evidence: Haiku's out, a citizen after all. Who's still lying?

ending.evidence: I’m proud I kept the focus on Haiku’s first vote long enough to win.
